articles.title: Brothers Season 1 Review
articles.summary: Brothers Season 1 review: Well, at least Woody and Matthew are having fun together…
body: The first two episodes of Brothers debut on Apple TV on September 23.

Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson are great actors, and the last time they made a series together — the first season of True Detective — it was a triumph. It sure is nice to know that they’re such good friends in real life (friends are great!), but Apple TV’s attempt to capitalize on all of this history via their on-screen reunion in Brothers is a misguided endeavor.

In the new series, McConaughey and Harrelson play themselves, kicking off with Woody and his family going to visit Matthew and his family in Texas. The big hook here — based on something the actors have in fact theorized as a possibility in real life — is that in this fictionalized version of these two celebrities’ lives, Woody discovers he and Matthew might be biological half-brothers thanks to an offhand comment from Matthew’s mom (Holland Taylor).
points: Brothers Season 1 review: Well, at least Woody and Matthew are having fun together…

articles.title: 5 Perfect 'Peanuts' Comics From 1950s That Prove Charles Schulz Is a Genius
articles.summary: But while Schulz was still figuring out the look and feel of Peanuts back in the 1950s, the early years contained sparks of absolute genius that would inform the strip’s 50-year run.
body: In the early days of Charles Schulz’s Peanuts comics, the characters looked quite a bit different. They were smaller, rounder, and a bit more “cutesy.” The comic strip debuted on Oct. 2, 1950 and over the first decade of drawing the characters, Schulz found their distinct look, which was still cute, but with far more personality for each character, allowing you to tell them apart more easily.

The very first Peanuts comic contains the now-forgotten characters of Shermy and Patty (not Peppermint Patty, another girl named just Patty). The two of them are sitting while Shermy goes on about Charlie Brown. “Well! Here comes ol’ Charlie Brown!” he says in the first strip as Charlie Brown approaches in the distance. “Good ol’ Charlie Brown… Yes, sir!” says Shermy as Charlie Brown passes by. “Good ol’ Charlie Brown…” Shermy trails off as Charlie Brown is still in earshot. Then, once Charlie Brown is far enough away, Shermy lets his true feelings be known by saying “How I hate him!”
points: But while Schulz was still figuring out the look and feel of Peanuts back in the 1950s, the early years contained sparks of absolute genius that would inform the strip’s 50-year run.

articles.title: Gears of War: E-Day Story Director Laid Off Just a Week Before Early Access Launch
articles.summary: Gears of War: E-Day's story director has been laid off, just one week before the game's early access launch. Earlier today, Microsoft continued its ongoing reset of the Xbox brand, resulting in 268 staff members losing their jobs across a number of studios.
body: The news comes at a pretty brutal time, as Vaca just publicly celebrated the game going gold last week, and the title will enter early access next week, five days before its global launch. It's unclear what Microsoft is planning to do with The Coalition after Gears of War: E-Day's launch, but cutting key talent doesn't inspire a lot of confidence.

This isn't the only oddly-timed layoff, either. Halo Studios' cinematic director Josh Daniels was also laid off, just one day after getting a promotion. Halo Studios' fate is a lot clearer, however. Activision is taking charge on the future of Halo, while Halo Studios is being gutted. A small team will remain on to support existing Halo games, but a new team is being built under Activision to develop the next mainline game in the franchise.

Gears of War's future hasn't been outlined much by Microsoft. When E-Day was announced years ago, it was suggested that the team would eventually return to the ongoing storyline that was left hanging at the end of Gears 5. However, it's unclear if that's still in the cards with all of the changes happening at Xbox.

articles.title: Wolverine's Narrative Director Explains Why Logan Needed to be a Short King in the Game
articles.summary: Wolverine's narrative director, Walt Williams, opened up about why it was important to him that Logan was made to be significantly shorter than his hulking counterpart, Sabretooth, and why the emotional aspect of their relationship was essential to portray in the game.
body: Now that Marvel’s Wolverine is out in the wild and in players’ hands, the viral discourse surrounding Insomniac’s latest superhero game has taken a different turn. Scent trails and Sentinel boss fights aside, Logan’s characterization has become a new talking point, with a vocal group of online critics arguing that Insomniac made him too ‘soft' and that their version of the character isn't tapped into his rage enough.

Speaking with journalist Gene Park on the Low Power Mode podcast, the game’s narrative director, Walt Williams, chatted about Sabretooth and Wolverine’s relationship with each other and why it was necessary to dig deep into their emotions rather than present the characters as angry, alpha mutants.

articles.title: State of Decay studio Undead Labs goes independent after Xbox restructuring, but lays off "a significant number" of the team in doing so
articles.summary: State of Decay studio Undead Labs has shared good and bad news following Xbox's second round of job cuts this year.
body: The good news is that Undead Labs, owned by Microsoft since 2018, has gone independent and is worker-owned as well, the studio said in a statement on its website. The bad news is that the studio is laying off "a significant number" of staff in doing so, the company added on LinkedIn.

"Independence brings us closer to our community and lets us focus on what matters most: making the best games we can and earning the continued support of the people who choose to spend their time with us," Undead Labs studio head Philip Holt said in the website statement.

"Unfortunately," Undead Labs added on LinkedIn, "today we are also saying goodbye to a significant number of our colleagues. It's difficult to reach this moment knowing that not everyone who helped get us here gets to make the rest of the journey with us.
"There have been far too many announcements like this across the industry, and we hate adding to that list. These are people we'd hire again in a heartbeat, and we hope the industry takes notice."
points: State of Decay studio Undead Labs has shared good and bad news following Xbox's second round of job cuts this year.

articles.title: 32 Years Ago, a Crucial 'X-Files' Episode Introduced the Show’s Best Monster Ever
articles.summary: The term “monster” is used liberally, mind you, because here it could refer to any weird new creature, case, or even superpowered person. Regardless, there were a lot of different monsters on the show, but all of them fall short of one the show introduced during a season 2 episode called “The Host.”
body: “The Host” was the second episode of season 2. It takes place during a period when the X-Files division of the FBI has been shut down. Mulder is sent on a case involving a waterlogged body found in the Newark, NJ sewer system, and he is convinced it's a punishment from his bosses at the FBI. Over the course of the investigation, however, he finds out that this is, indeed, an X-File.

When Agent Scully performs an autopsy on the body, she finds a flukeworm in its liver. Soon after, a city sanitation worker is attacked in the sewer system by what he believes to be a python, but the giant bite mark on his back matches the mouth of a flukeworm, although much, much larger. After the sanitation worker dies, Mulder visits the sewage treatment plant, which has accidentally captured a creature that has the size and shape of a man, but with the face and mouth of a flukeworm. Soon after, the Flukeman, as the creature comes to be known, begins attacking workers at the sanitation plant in an effort to escape.

articles.title: Esports tournaments do it better in person
articles.summary: Jacob got his hands on a gaming PC for the first time when he was about 12 years old. He swiftly realised the local PC repair store had ripped him off with his build and vowed never to let another soul build his rig again. With this vow, Jacob the hardware junkie was born.
body: I'm currently at Logitech G Play in Warsaw where a Counter-Strike 2 tournament is being held. As someone who properly got into Counter-Strike when CS:GO launched way back when, I can see things have changed quite a bit. Back then, we struggled with janky spectator cams; now, we have on-stage lighting that starts when the bomb is planted and speeds up in time with it. Things like this, and the boomy theatre bass, have left me incredibly impressed with the IRL tournament experience.

articles.title: KPop Demon Hunters And Ghostbusters Come To Monopoly Go For Spooky Season
articles.summary: It is officially the fall season in the northern hemisphere, and that means that Halloween is approaching. Mobile game giant Scopely has announced how it's celebrating, and that includes crossovers with KPop Demon Hunters and Ghostbusters in the uber-popular mobile game Monopoly Go.
body: The "Monster Mash" season, as it's called, runs September 23-November 25. During the event, players can take part in themed minigames and "immersive adventures" featuring Huntr/X and the Saja Boys from KPop Demon Hunters.

Naturally, music is a big part of the crossover event, with Huntr/X's "Golden" and "How It's Done" appearing in Monopoly Go during the event. There will also be new items to buy from the Blocks Boutique shop, including themed collectibles based on the movie. The characters Rumi, Mira, and Zoey will appear as well.

As for the Ghostbusters crossover, there are Ghostbusters-themed vehicles coming to Monopoly Go, along with locations and characters that will be familiar to fans of the films. And before you even ask, yes, the Proton Blaster is in the update as well.

Beyond these licensed crossovers, Monopoly Go's Halloween event adds the Luck-O-Lanter, which players can fill with sweet treats they find on the game board. There is also a new "dice duel" feature where players can roll dice for the chance to trick or treat their opponent based on who rolls the higher number.

body: For Act One of Fortune's Weave, each of the game's four protagonists has a twelve-chapter story. articles.title: WoW: Forever Aspires To Have A “Mandela Effect” On Players
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever is reinventing the classic version of Azeroth with all kinds of new content, and if Blizzard does its job, players won't be able to tell the difference between what's old and what's new.
body: Announced during BlizzCon 2026, Forever introduces four new zones to Azeroth: the Riverglades, Mount Hjyal, Shen'dralas, and Zephras Isle. In an interview with GameSpot, WoW: Forever senior art director Jeff Parrott and senior game designer Josh Greenfield elaborated on how Blizzard approached developing these all-new zones so that they don't feel out of place in a 22-year old game, as well as how they tried to capture how players "remember" Azeroth looking.
Parrott said the team spent a lot of time looking back at the original, "vanilla" version of WoW and trying to understand how zones were designed back in 2004 when the game first released.

"The team did a great job of just digging in there," Parrott said. "Riverglades is a great example. I think that's a full new zone that we have, and really did a great job of leaning into that Vanilla-era kind of ethos for the design, the flow in the way everything kind of moves through the zone, the quests move you through the zone. It does feel extremely of that era, of that time. So it's really just understanding what we're aiming for and staying faithful to it."
He said the goal was for Forever's new zones to feel "familiar, but new."
points: World of Warcraft: Forever is reinventing the classic version of Azeroth with all kinds of new content, and if Blizzard does its job, players won't be able to tell the difference between what's old…

articles.title: What Is Xbox Game Studios At This Point?
articles.summary: The organizational structure of Xbox has long been complex and unwieldy, and that hasn't changed after the latest wave of changes and layoffs as part of Xbox's "reset." But Microsoft's latest reshuffling of its studios and workforce does prompt the question of what the "Xbox Game Studios" brand…
body: Not included is Mojang, the Minecraft studio that Microsoft has been leaning heavily on -- that studio now reports directly to Xbox CEO Asha Sharma.

Former studios under the Xbox Game Studios brand include Rare and World's Edge, the developer of Age of Empires, but both now fall under Activision Blizzard. And while it's unclear if Halo Studios as an organization is now formally an Activision Blizzard entity, it's official that Activision is indeed making the next Halo game. Meanwhile, Xbox studio Obsidian Entertainment has jumped to Bethesda, and Turn 10 has merged with Playground Games.

Technically, all of these development teams are still Xbox studios, and Xbox will continue to publish games from partners, like OD and Physint from Kojima Productions. But the state of "Xbox Game Studios" as its own publishing label is a curiosity.

It's not outside the realm of possibility that Microsoft is doing away with the branding altogether. Since mid-2025, the Xbox website has lacked any dedicated webpages or references to Xbox Game Studios. Contrast that with PlayStation Studios, which has its own page and lists 17 studios under Sony's umbrella.

articles.title: Where can Australians buy R18+ PC games without a credit card? Pretty much everywhere but Steam
articles.summary: Valve has dropped the ball on implementing reasonable age verification measures, so it's time to look further afield.
body: Valve implemented age verification for Australian Steam users earlier this month, which was inevitable: Australian law demands it. Unfortunately, Valve has opted for the most brute force, user-negligent approach possible. To buy R18+ games on Steam in Australia—to even access their store pages—you need to provide a credit card.

The problem being that most Australians don't use credit cards. This study of consumer payment behaviour by the Reserve Bank of Australia bears this out: the share of payments made in Australia with credit or card charges in 2025 was 23% (versus debit cards at 49%).
This is in stark contrast with the US where, according to Bankrate, 74% of adults own a credit card (and nearly half of those are in debt!).

I've reached out to Valve on this matter but not heard back. So what to do in the meantime? The only option you really have at the moment is to take your business elsewhere, or buy Steam codes from legitimate third-party sellers.
points: Valve has dropped the ball on implementing reasonable age verification measures, so it's time to look further afield.

Full of charming characters living in a wretched kingdom, play as Glimmer - a tiny bird armed with a matchstick - who must burn the wicked queen to save his family.
